mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies anticipate lower revenues.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a single month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and efficiency.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between HOUST and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month period of CPIAUCSL inflation above 3% signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL above 3% and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected sharp decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies benefit from increased economic activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
